title: The Wild Salt
premise: Ada Zhou has spent nine years copying prayers he no longer believes, hiding his smuggler's knowledge of the Thornfell passes behind a scribe's ink-stained hands. When the old gods stir and answer a dying woman's plea through his own mouth, Ada becomes the unwilling vessel of Salt-Mother Yara—and the only person who can see that King Aldric's crown is a parasite wearing him. Hunted by the crown's inquisitors and shadowed by his former smuggling partner turned bounty hunter, Ada must carry the god up the forbidden mountain where she was bound centuries ago. In the end, unbinding the king means choosing between the truth that will shatter the temple that sheltered him and the loyalty of the friend who dies buying him time; Ada speaks the truth, frees both king and god, and finally claims a name and place of his own.
about_author: Emrys Thackeray is the pen name of a former cartographer who once mapped smuggling routes through real mountain ranges before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who know too many secret roads and too few safe ones.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Ada Zhou's POV. We meet Ada copying prayers in the temple of Thornfell, secretly trading on his knowledge of smuggler roads to pay down his family's debt. A dying washerwoman grabs his sleeve and begs the old gods for mercy—and Ada's mouth answers in a voice not his own. Emotional beat: dread at being seen for the first time.

chapters.title: The God in His Throat
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The voice identifies itself as Yara, the Salt-Mother, bound beneath the mountain for three hundred years. She shows Ada visions: King Aldric's crown is a fragment of her captor, feeding on the king. Ada tries to deny everything, but the temple's high priest notices the miracle. Emotional beat: denial curdling into reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wears
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Queen-Sister Maren. Maren suspects her brother is no longer wholly himself—Aldric signs decrees in his sleep and his eyes have gone salt-white. She travels to Thornfell seeking answers, colliding with Ada just as the crown's inquisitors arrive to arrest 'the vessel.' Emotional beat: two lonely watchers recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Fleeing the inquisitors, Ada uses his smuggler knowledge to slip into the mountains with Maren and Yara's growing presence inside him. But the first pass is watched by Sefa, Ada's old partner-in-smuggling, now a bounty hunter who feels betrayed by his disappearance years ago. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility—everyone he vanished from now hunts him.

chapters.title: Salt and Iron
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa captures Ada but hesitates when Yara heals a wound Ada took protecting Maren. Flashbacks reveal their shared past and why Ada went silent: he informed on their crew under torture, and shame made him hide. Sefa lets them go—but warns the inquisitors already know the mountain routes. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against old wounds.

chapters.title: The Temple's Ledger
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Sheltering in an abandoned shrine, they find records proving the temple didn't bind Yara to imprison her—it bound her to keep the crown-thing asleep, and the binding is failing because the temple stopped believing. Maren realizes her own church built the cage and let it rust. Emotional beat: faith cracking under the weight of institutional lies.

chapters.title: The Thing in the Hall
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The crown-thing, aware of them now, sends Aldric's army and twists Sefa's debt into a trap: betray Ada or watch her crew hang. At a mountain waystation, Ada confronts Sefa one last time and confesses his oldest sin aloud—the truth he'd hidden even from himself. Emotional beat: confession as liberation, even as it breaks his heart.

chapters.title: Where the Mountain Was Bound
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax part one. They reach the deep shrine where Yara was chained. To unbind her fully, a mortal must speak the whole truth of the binding aloud—every lie the temple told, every name erased. Ada begins the speaking as the crown-thing floods the mountain with Aldric's soldiers. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Sefa arrives—not to betray Ada but to hold the pass alone against the army, buying minutes with her life. Ada finishes the true names; Yara rises like a tide, tearing the parasite from Aldric's crown across the miles. The king wakes weeping in his hall as the thing burns out of the gold. Emotional beat: sacrifice and release intertwined.

chapters.title: A Name of His Own
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, resolution. The debt-ledgers burn; the temple must reckon publicly with its lies, and Maren stays to reform it while Aldric, diminished but human, abdicates some power to her. Yara offers Ada a place as her speaker, but he chooses something smaller and harder: staying in Thornfell, visible, known, forgiven. Sefa survives, scarred, and comes home. Emotional beat: belonging finally chosen, not hidden into.
